elements.doc: One model holds the needs, requirements, application structure, infrastructure and verifications of a product, with links between them.
elements.name: oneModel

elements.doc: Code generation is deterministic.
elements.name: deterministicGeneration

elements.doc: The model is correct before code generation starts.
elements.name: correctModel

elements.doc: Each requirement traces to the code, infrastructure and tests that cover it.
elements.name: traceability

elements.doc: The model does not depend on one cloud provider.
elements.name: cloudIndependence

elements.doc: Each application generator must read only the IR.
elements.name: app001

elements.doc: For each application in the IR, the generator of its target must write the code in the output folder that the configuration file gives for that application.
elements.name: app002

elements.doc: A generator must write code only for the entities, operations, views and roles in the IR, and for the health endpoint of PRD-APP-012.
elements.name: app003

elements.doc: A FastAPI or Next.js application must also write an OpenAPI 3.1 document, openapi.gen.json, from the IR. The OpenAPI document that the running service supplies must agree with it.
elements.name: app004

elements.doc: The client types of a React application and the schemas of the API that it calls must come from the same IR entities and operations. A contract test in the toolchain CI must compare the generated client with the openapi.gen.json of the called application.
elements.name: app005

elements.doc: Phase 2: a React application can call an external API that an imported OpenAPI file gives, in place of an application in the model.
elements.name: app006

elements.doc: Each application must authenticate users with the Amazon Cognito user pool of its environment. Web clients must use Cognito managed login with the authorization code flow and PKCE.
elements.name: app007

elements.doc: For each operation, the generated server code must examine the access token. It must return HTTP 401 if there is no valid token, and HTTP 403 if no group in the cognito:groups claim is in allowedRoles. An operation with public = true must need no token.
elements.name: app008

elements.doc: The generated web client must show only the navigation items and views that the roles of the user permit. It must send a user with no session to the login page. The server check of PRD-APP-008 stays the protection.
elements.name: app009

elements.doc: Each application must read its environment values at run time, not at build time. One build or one container image must operate in all environments.
elements.name: app010

elements.doc: Each application must get secret values from environment variables that ECS sets from Secrets Manager. Generated code must not contain a secret value.
elements.name: app011

elements.doc: A FastAPI or Next.js application must supply GET /healthz with no authentication. It must return HTTP 200 while the process operates.
elements.name: app012

elements.doc: The Dockerfile of a FastAPI or Next.js application must use a multi-stage build and a base image pinned by digest. The container must run as a user that is not root and must not contain a secret value.
elements.name: app013

elements.doc: API errors must use problem details (RFC 9457) with the media type application/problem+json.
elements.name: app014

elements.doc: Server logs must be JSON lines on standard output, with a request ID in each line. Logs must not contain tokens or secret values.
elements.name: app015

elements.doc: The generated code of each target must pass dsml check-output with no error.
elements.name: app016

elements.doc: Each generated source file must have the trace header that the traceability PRD gives.
elements.name: app017

elements.doc: The FastAPI target must use Python, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, SQLAlchemy 2, Alembic and pytest, and uv must manage the project. The versions must come from the version baseline.
elements.name: app101

elements.doc: The generator must write one slice folder for each operation: app/features/<entity>/<operation>/. A slice must contain endpoint_gen.py (the router) and schemas_gen.py (the Pydantic models).
elements.name: app102

elements.doc: For a CRUD operation, the generator must write the handler as handler_gen.py. For a custom operation, it must write handler.py as a create-once stub.
elements.name: app103

elements.doc: Code that all slices use must be in app/shared/: the database session, the SQLAlchemy models, the Cognito token check, the configuration and the error types.
elements.name: app104

elements.doc: app/main_gen.py must create the FastAPI application and register the router of each slice in sorted order.
elements.name: app105

elements.doc: A generated file in a slice must import only from its own slice and from app/shared/.
elements.name: app106

elements.doc: Each operation in the IR must have one endpoint with the HTTP method and the path of the operation. CRUD operations must use the default methods and paths in the table of the section "API operations and schemas" unless the model gives a different method or path.
elements.name: app110

elements.doc: For each exposed entity, the generator must write Pydantic v2 models for create input, update input and output. The key field must not be in the create input. Each field of the update input must be optional.
elements.name: app111

elements.doc: Field rules must become Pydantic field constraints: minLength and maxLength to min_length and max_length, minValue and maxValue to ge and le, and pattern to pattern.
elements.name: app112

elements.doc: A request that breaks a field rule must get HTTP 422. A request that breaks a unique rule must get HTTP 409. A request for an entity that does not exist must get HTTP 404.
elements.name: app113

elements.doc: A list operation must accept limit (default 50, maximum 200) and offset (default 0). It must return the found entities in items, sorted by key, and their count in total.
elements.name: app114

elements.doc: An output schema must give a related entity as its key, not as a nested object.
elements.name: app115

elements.doc: For a custom operation, the generated endpoint must validate the input, check the roles, open a database session and then call handle(input, session, user) in handler.py. It must return the output that handle gives as the output schema.
elements.name: app116

elements.doc: The create-once handler.py stub must contain the typed handle function. Its body must raise NotImplementedError, so the endpoint returns HTTP 501 until a developer writes the logic.
elements.name: app117

elements.doc: For each entity, the generator must write one typed SQLAlchemy 2 model in app/shared/db/models/<entity>_gen.py. The table name must be the entity name in snake case.
elements.name: app120

elements.doc: Field types must map to PostgreSQL types as the table of the section "Data access and migrations" gives.
elements.name: app121

elements.doc: A [*] to [*] relation must have a generated join table. A [0..1] or [1] relation must have a foreign key.
elements.name: app122

elements.doc: Database access must use the SQLAlchemy mode and the database driver that decision record 03 gives.
elements.name: app123

elements.doc: The generator must keep the schema snapshot in .dsml/schema-snapshot.json. If the IR schema is different from the snapshot, the generator must write one new Alembic migration and then update the snapshot.
elements.name: app124

elements.doc: A migration file must have the name migrations/versions/<NNNN>_<slug>_gen.py. Its revision ID must come from its content and its number, not from a random value or the clock.
elements.name: app125

elements.doc: The generator must keep each migration file that it wrote before, byte for byte.
elements.name: app126

elements.doc: The generator must not write a migration that drops or renames a table or a column, unless the IR has the #Destructive metadata for that change.
elements.name: app127

elements.doc: app/migrate_gen.py must apply all migrations that the database does not have, and then stop. The deployment runs it as decision record 03 gives.
elements.name: app128

elements.doc: app/shared/auth/cognito_gen.py must supply a FastAPI dependency. It must check the signature of the access token against the JWKS of the user pool, and the claims iss, token_use (access), client_id and exp.
elements.name: app130

elements.doc: The dependency must keep the JWKS in memory and get it again only when a token has an unknown key ID.
elements.name: app131

elements.doc: app/shared/config_gen.py must read the configuration from environment variables at start. If a mandatory variable is missing, the application must stop with a message that names the variable.
elements.name: app132

elements.doc: The Dockerfile must install the locked dependencies with uv sync --frozen --no-dev and run Uvicorn on port 8000.
elements.name: app133

elements.doc: The fixed-name generated files of the FastAPI target must be: pyproject.toml, Dockerfile, .dockerignore, alembic.ini, migrations/env.py and each __init__.py in a generated folder.
elements.name: app134

elements.doc: pytest must run on the generated project with no error when the project has no tests.
elements.name: app135

elements.doc: The React target must use strict TypeScript, pnpm, Vite, React, TanStack Router, TanStack Query, TanStack Form, Zod, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui and Amplify Auth. The versions must come from the version baseline.
elements.name: app201

elements.doc: The generator must put the code in the FSD layers app, pages, widgets, features, entities and shared in src/.
elements.name: app202

elements.doc: Generated code must obey the FSD import rules: a module imports only from lower layers, and only through the public API of a slice.
elements.name: app203

elements.doc: Each slice must have a create-once index.ts that re-exports the generated index.gen.ts.
elements.name: app204

elements.doc: The path alias @/ must refer to src/.
elements.name: app205

elements.doc: Slice names and file names must be the kebab case of the model element names.
elements.name: app206

elements.doc: The generator must put each model element in the slice and the files that the table of the section "Map from model elements to FSD layers" gives.
elements.name: app210

elements.doc: The Zod schemas of an entity must apply the same field rules as the Pydantic models of PRD-APP-112.
elements.name: app211

elements.doc: The generator must write the shadcn/ui components that the templates use into shared/ui as create-once files, from the pinned copy in the toolchain package.
elements.name: app212

elements.doc: The generator must write the TanStack Router route tree with code-based routing in src/app/router/routes.gen.tsx. The project must not use the TanStack Router file-based routing plugin.
elements.name: app220

elements.doc: Each view must have one route. A list view must use the path /<entities>, a detail view /<entities>/$id, and a form view /<operation>.
elements.name: app221

elements.doc: The beforeLoad function of each route must check the session and the roles of the view. With no session, it must start the login. With no permitted role, it must show a "not permitted" page.
elements.name: app222

elements.doc: The loader of each list and detail route must load its data with queryClient.ensureQueryData and the query options of the entity slice.
elements.name: app223

elements.doc: Each query key must be an array in the form [<entity>, <operation>, <parameters>].
elements.name: app224

elements.doc: After a mutation, the generated code must invalidate the queries of the changed entity.
elements.name: app225

elements.doc: Each form must use TanStack Form with the Zod schema of its operation as the validator. Each field must use the shadcn/ui form components, with a label and an error message.
elements.name: app226

elements.doc: The client must show a problem details response as an error message with its title and detail.
elements.name: app227

elements.doc: Each table must have column headers, and the user must be able to reach each control with the keyboard.
elements.name: app228

elements.doc: Before the first render, the application must read /config.json. The file must give the API base URL, the AWS Region, the user pool ID, the app client ID and the managed login domain.
elements.name: app230

elements.doc: shared/auth/amplify.gen.ts must configure Amplify Auth from the runtime configuration and use Cognito managed login with PKCE.
elements.name: app231

elements.doc: The API client must add the access token of the session to each request as a bearer token.
elements.name: app232

elements.doc: pnpm build must write the static files to dist/. The build must not contain environment values.
elements.name: app233

elements.doc: The generator must write a Steiger configuration, and dsml check-output must run Steiger with no error.
elements.name: app234

elements.doc: The fixed-name generated files of the React target must be: package.json, tsconfig.json, vite.config.ts, index.html, components.json and steiger.config.ts.
elements.name: app235

elements.doc: The Next.js target must use strict TypeScript, pnpm, Next.js with the App Router, React, TanStack Query, TanStack Form, Zod, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, Drizzle ORM and Amplify Auth with its Next.js adapter. The versions must come from the version baseline.
elements.name: app301

elements.doc: The Next.js app/ folder must be at the project root and hold only route files that re-export from src/. The generator must own the full app/ folder.
elements.name: app302

elements.doc: The FSD layers must be in src/, and the layers app and pages must have the names _app and _pages.
elements.name: app303

elements.doc: The generator must map model elements to slices as PRD-APP-210 gives, with the layer names of PRD-APP-303.
elements.name: app304

elements.doc: A slice must export server-only modules through index.server.ts and other modules through index.ts. Each server-only module must import server-only.
elements.name: app305

elements.doc: The generated code must obey the FSD import rules of PRD-APP-203, and dsml check-output must run Steiger with no error.
elements.name: app306

elements.doc: For each operation, the generator must write a route handler in src/_app/api-routes/<operation>.gen.ts. A generated app/api/<path>/route.ts must re-export it.
elements.name: app310

elements.doc: The REST contract must be the contract of the FastAPI target (PRD-APP-110 to PRD-APP-115), with the path prefix /api.
elements.name: app311

elements.doc: A route handler must validate the input with the Zod schema of the operation, check the token and the roles, call the server function of the operation and return JSON or problem details.
elements.name: app312

elements.doc: For a CRUD operation, the generator must write the server function as features/<operation>/api/<operation>.server.gen.ts. For a custom operation, it must write <operation>.server.ts as a create-once stub that throws an error with the HTTP status 501.
elements.name: app313

elements.doc: Server components of pages must call the server functions for read and list directly, with no HTTP request. Client components must call the route handlers through TanStack Query.
elements.name: app314

elements.doc: For each view, the generator must write a page slice in src/_pages/<view> and a generated app/<route>/page.tsx that re-exports it. Routes must use the paths of PRD-APP-221.
elements.name: app320

elements.doc: Each form must be a client component that uses TanStack Form with the Zod schema of its operation. The route handler must validate the same input again with the same schema.
elements.name: app321

elements.doc: Authentication must use Amplify Auth with its Next.js adapter, and the adapter must keep the tokens in cookies.
elements.name: app322

elements.doc: The generated request interceptor (middleware.ts or proxy.ts, as the pinned Next.js version requires) must send a request for a protected page with no session to the login.
elements.name: app323

elements.doc: Server components and route handlers must get the session through the Amplify adapter and apply the role checks of PRD-APP-008.
elements.name: app324

elements.doc: The root layout must give the public runtime values (Region, user pool ID, app client ID, login domain) to client components from server-side environment variables. The build must not use NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables.
elements.name: app325

elements.doc: The generator must write the Drizzle schema of all entities in src/shared/db/schema.gen.ts, with the type map of PRD-APP-121.
elements.name: app330

elements.doc: The generator must write each migration from the difference between .dsml/schema-snapshot.json and the IR, in the file format that the Drizzle migrator reads. The project must not use drizzle-kit generate.
elements.name: app331

elements.doc: PRD-APP-125 to PRD-APP-128 must also apply to the Next.js target. The migration command must be node migrate.gen.mjs.
elements.name: app332

elements.doc: The Next.js build must use the standalone output. The Dockerfile must run the server on port 3000.
elements.name: app333

elements.doc: The fixed-name generated files of the Next.js target must be: package.json, tsconfig.json, next.config.ts, the full app/ folder, middleware.ts or proxy.ts, drizzle.config.ts, components.json, steiger.config.ts, Dockerfile and .dockerignore.
elements.name: app334

elements.doc: The generator must write .github/workflows/pr.gen.yml, main.gen.yml and promote.gen.yml with the triggers and jobs in the table of the section "Workflows and jobs".
elements.name: cicd001

elements.doc: pr.gen.yml must run dsml validate and upload the SARIF findings to GitHub code scanning.
elements.name: cicd002

elements.doc: pr.gen.yml must run dsml generate --check and fail if a generated file is different from the committed file.
elements.name: cicd003

elements.doc: For each application, pr.gen.yml must install the dependencies from the committed lockfile (uv sync --frozen or pnpm install --frozen-lockfile), then run the linter, the type checker and the tests. A lockfile that does not agree with the dependency list must make the job fail.
elements.name: cicd004

elements.doc: pr.gen.yml must run dsml check-output.
elements.name: cicd005

elements.doc: pr.gen.yml must run tofu plan for dev with the plan role, and write the plan text in the job summary. It must not apply.
elements.name: cicd006

elements.doc: main.gen.yml must build each container image and the static files of each React application one time. It must then deploy them to dev.
elements.name: cicd007

elements.doc: promote.gen.yml must deploy the image digests and the static files of one main build to staging, then to prod. It must not build again.
elements.name: cicd008

elements.doc: Each deploy job must use a concurrency group for its environment, so only one deployment runs in an environment at a time. A new run must not cancel a running deployment.
elements.name: cicd009

elements.doc: Workflows must get AWS credentials only through GitHub OIDC and the roles of PRD-IAC-027 and PRD-IAC-028. They must not use long-term access keys.
elements.name: cicd010

elements.doc: Each job must declare the smallest permissions set that it needs. Only jobs that use AWS must have id-token: write.
elements.name: cicd011

elements.doc: Each deploy job must use the GitHub environment of its target environment (dev, staging or prod).
elements.name: cicd012

elements.doc: The generator must write a README with the settings that a repository administrator must make: the GitHub environments, required reviewers for prod, and branch protection for the main branch.
elements.name: cicd013

elements.doc: Each third-party action must be pinned to a full commit SHA from the version baseline, with its version in a comment.
elements.name: cicd014

elements.doc: Workflows must not write secret values to logs or job summaries. Values from AWS outputs that are not secret can appear in summaries.
elements.name: cicd015

elements.doc: A deploy job must run tofu apply with the image digests of the build and model_commit set to the commit of the build.
elements.name: cicd016

elements.doc: After the apply, the job must run the migration task definition of each application with a database as a one-off ECS task, and wait for it. If the task fails, the job must stop before it changes a service.
elements.name: cicd017

elements.doc: After the migrations, the job must set each ECS service to its new task definition and wait for a steady state. If the ECS deployment circuit breaker rolls back, the job must fail.
elements.name: cicd018

elements.doc: Phase 2: for each React application, the job must upload the static files to its S3 bucket, write /config.json from the outputs of the root module, and invalidate the CloudFront cache.
elements.name: cicd019

elements.doc: promote.gen.yml must deploy to prod only after the staging deployment of the same build succeeded and a required reviewer approved the prod environment.
elements.name: cicd020

elements.doc: Each deploy job must write a job summary with the environment, the image digests, the model commit and the applied migrations.
elements.name: cicd021

elements.doc: The command dsml must have the seven subcommands init, validate, generate, trace, ir, check-output and version, with the options in the table of the section "Command line interface".
elements.name: core001

elements.doc: Each subcommand must stop with exit code 0 if it finds no error, 1 if it finds an error finding or a --check difference, and 2 if a usage error or an internal error occurs.
elements.name: core002

elements.doc: dsml generate must validate the model first. If there is an error finding, it must stop and write no file.
elements.name: core003

elements.doc: dsml generate --check must write no file. It must list each file that a normal run would add, change or delete.
elements.name: core004

elements.doc: dsml generate must generate only one part of the output when the user gives --application <name>, --infrastructure or --pipelines.
elements.name: core005

elements.doc: Each subcommand must write its report to standard output, or to the file that --output gives.
elements.name: core006

elements.doc: A message about a model location must give the file path, the line and the column.
elements.name: core007

elements.doc: Messages to the user must use ASD-STE100 Issue 9.
elements.name: core008

elements.doc: A subcommand must not ask for input from a terminal.
elements.name: core009

elements.doc: The option --verbose must write debug messages to standard error.
elements.name: core010

elements.doc: dsml check-output must run tsc, ruff, tofu validate, tflint and the FSD linter Steiger on the generated code of the selected targets. It must report a missing tool as an error with the tool name.
elements.name: core011

elements.doc: The toolchain must read its configuration from dsml.toml in the repository root, or from the file that the option --config gives.
elements.name: core012

elements.doc: The configuration file must give: the model files or folders; the output folder of each application, of the infrastructure and of the pipelines; the ID patterns; the optional rule sets; the default trace baseline; and the IaC options for one tool only.
elements.name: core013

elements.doc: The configuration file must have a schema version. The toolchain must report an unknown key or an unknown schema version as an error.
elements.name: core014

elements.doc: Environment variables, the user name, the host name, the locale, the time zone and the clock must not change the generated output.
elements.name: core015

elements.doc: The configuration file must not contain secret values.
elements.name: core016

elements.doc: The toolchain must call OpenSysML through the opensysml Python client. The client must start sysml-grpc as a private child process.
elements.name: core017

elements.doc: The toolchain must pin one OpenSysML version for the Python package and the sysml-grpc binary. The version must come from the version baseline.
elements.name: core018

elements.doc: At start, the toolchain must compare the version of sysml-grpc with the pinned version. If they are different, it must stop with exit code 2.
elements.name: core019

elements.doc: Only the IR adapter module must import the opensysml package. A lint rule in the toolchain CI must enforce this.
elements.name: core020

elements.doc: The adapter must convert each OpenSysML diagnostic into a finding of the category SYN of the validation PRD.
elements.name: core021

elements.doc: The IR must be JSON. The toolchain package must contain the JSON Schema of the IR.
elements.name: core022

elements.doc: The IR must have a semantic version in the field irVersion. A change that removes or renames a field must increase the major version.
elements.name: core023

elements.doc: The IR must hold each element of the five layers, its DSML attributes, its trace links and its source location (file, line, column).
elements.name: core024

elements.doc: The IR must not contain an OpenSysML type, an OpenSysML object or an OpenSysML internal ID.
elements.name: core025

elements.doc: Validators and generators must read only the IR. They get the results of formal constraints from the IR (PRD-CORE-054), not from OpenSysML.
elements.name: core026

elements.doc: The toolchain CI must compare the IR of each reference model with a stored golden IR file. A change of the OpenSysML version must pass this comparison before a release.
elements.name: core027

elements.doc: The same model, configuration file and toolchain version must give byte-identical generated files, IR, reports and trace manifests on each supported operating system.
elements.name: core028

elements.doc: The toolchain CI must run each reference model on Linux x64, and compare the outputs byte by byte with the golden files.
elements.name: core029

elements.doc: The toolchain CI must compare the output of each reference model with stored golden files.
elements.name: core030

elements.doc: Generators must write each list in an output file in a defined order: by element identity, then by name.
elements.name: core031

elements.doc: The output must not depend on the order of the model files on disk or in the configuration file.
elements.name: core032

elements.doc: The output must not contain a timestamp, a random value, an absolute path, a user name or a host name.
elements.name: core033

elements.doc: Each output file must use UTF-8 with no byte order mark, LF line ends and one LF at the end of the file.
elements.name: core034

elements.doc: Templates must give their output in the format of the pinned formatter for the file type: Prettier for TypeScript, ruff format for Python, tofu fmt for HCL. The generator must not run a formatter. The toolchain CI must run each formatter in check mode on the golden files and find no change.
elements.name: core035

elements.doc: The generator must not write lockfiles (uv.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, .terraform.lock.hcl). The generated CI makes them, and Git keeps them.
elements.name: core036

elements.doc: A minor or patch release of the toolchain must not change the output for an unchanged model, except to fix a defect that its release notes name.
elements.name: core037

elements.doc: The header of a generated file must give the major version of the toolchain only.
elements.name: core038

elements.doc: A generated file must have a name that ends with .gen.<ext> or _gen.py, or be on the fixed-name list of its target. Each generation PRD gives its fixed-name list, for example pyproject.toml, package.json, Dockerfile and the Next.js app/ folder.
elements.name: core039

elements.doc: The generator must keep a manifest in .dsml/generated.json. For each generated file, it must give the path and the SHA-256 hash. For each create-once file, it must give the path.
elements.name: core040

elements.doc: At each run, the generator must delete each generated file of the old manifest that the new run does not write.
elements.name: core041

elements.doc: The generator must not write, change or delete a file that is not a generated file of the old or new manifest, except a new create-once file.
elements.name: core042

elements.doc: If the hash of a generated file is different from its hash in the manifest, dsml generate must stop with an error that lists the changed files. The option --overwrite must replace them.
elements.name: core043

elements.doc: The generator must write a create-once file only if no file exists at its path.
elements.name: core044

elements.doc: Generated code must call hand-written code through a typed interface, for example a handler function with typed parameters. A difference between the two must cause a type check error.
elements.name: core045

elements.doc: The generator must own the dependency lists of each target. A developer must add a dependency in the configuration file, not in a generated file.
elements.name: core046

elements.doc: The toolchain must be a Python package that uv builds. The release process must attach it to the GitHub release of the toolchain. A user must be able to install it with uv tool install.
elements.name: core047

elements.doc: The package must contain the DSML library, the IR schema, the templates and the pinned copy of the shadcn/ui components.
elements.name: core048

elements.doc: The installation must supply the sysml-grpc binary of the pinned OpenSysML version and check its SHA-256 hash against the release checksums of OpenSysML.
elements.name: core049

elements.doc: The toolchain must supply a GitHub Action that installs a pinned toolchain version and runs one subcommand.
elements.name: core050

elements.doc: When its input sarif is true, the GitHub Action must upload the SARIF findings to GitHub code scanning.
elements.name: core051

elements.doc: Toolchain releases must use semantic versioning. The release notes must name each change to the generated output.
elements.name: core052

elements.doc: Before each release, the toolchain CI must generate and deploy each reference model to a sandbox AWS account, and remove it after the test.
elements.name: core053

elements.doc: The adapter must evaluate each formal constraint of a requirement through OpenSysML, one time for each environment, and write each result into the IR. The evaluation uses the attribute values of that environment. A result is true, false or unknown. An unknown result gives the features that have no value.
elements.name: core054

elements.doc: The DSML must be a SysML v2 model library package with the name DSML.
elements.name: dsml001

elements.doc: The DSML must extend SysML v2 only with metadata definitions, attribute definitions and enumeration definitions. It must not add a concrete syntax.
elements.name: dsml002

elements.doc: Each DSML element kind must be available as a user-defined keyword, for example #Need, #Entity and #ContainerService.
elements.name: dsml003

elements.doc: OpenSysML must parse and resolve the DSML library with no error and no warning.
elements.name: dsml004

elements.doc: The DSML library must use only SysML v2 constructs that the OMG pilot implementation also accepts.
elements.name: dsml005

elements.doc: The toolchain package must include the DSML library, so a model needs no download.
elements.name: dsml006

elements.doc: A model must be a set of .sysml files in one Git repository. The toolchain configuration file must give the files or folders of the model.
elements.name: dsml007

elements.doc: A model must import the DSML library with private import DSML::*; or refer to its elements with qualified names.
elements.name: dsml008

elements.doc: Each DSML keyword of an element kind must be a metadata definition that specializes Metaobjects::SemanticMetadata. Its base type must hold the attributes of the element kind. A keyword on a dependency, and a metadata definition that holds its own attributes, must be a plain metadata definition.
elements.name: dsml009

elements.doc: The model must give attribute values with redefinitions of the base type features, for example :>> priority = Priority::must;.
elements.name: dsml010

elements.doc: A stakeholder must be a part definition with the keyword #Stakeholder.
elements.name: dsml011

elements.doc: A need must be a concern usage with the keyword #Need. It must have one or more stakeholder members that refer to a stakeholder.
elements.name: dsml012

elements.doc: A need must have these attributes: ID (the short name), title, text (the doc comment), priority and status.
elements.name: dsml013

elements.doc: A requirement must be a requirement usage with the keyword #Requirement. It can frame one or more needs with frame.
elements.name: dsml014

elements.doc: A requirement must have these attributes: ID (the short name), title, text (the doc comment), kind, priority and status. It can also have rationale, source and owner.
elements.name: dsml015

elements.doc: The DSML must define these enumerations. Priority: must, should, could, wont. Status: draft, approved, implemented, verified, retired. RequirementKind: functional, performance, security, interface, constraint.
elements.name: dsml016

elements.doc: A requirement derivation must use the #derivation connection of the SysML v2 RequirementDerivation library. A refinement must use a dependency with the #refinement metadata of the SysML v2 ModelingMetadata library.
elements.name: dsml017

elements.doc: A requirement can contain formal constraints (require constraint) that refer to attributes of model elements. Quantities must use the SysML v2 quantity and unit libraries.
elements.name: dsml018

elements.doc: A project can add attributes to needs and requirements with a project library that specializes the DSML base types.
elements.name: dsml019

elements.doc: An application must be a part usage with the keyword #Application. Its attribute target must have one of the values fastapi, react or nextjs.
elements.name: dsml020

elements.doc: A model can contain more than one application.
elements.name: dsml021

elements.doc: An entity must be a part definition with the keyword #Entity. Each attribute usage of an entity is a field.
elements.name: dsml022

elements.doc: A field type must be one of: String, Integer, Boolean, Real from the SysML v2 libraries; Decimal, Date, DateTime and Uuid from the DSML library; or an enumeration definition in the model.
elements.name: dsml023

elements.doc: An entity must have one primary key field with the keyword #Key.
elements.name: dsml024

elements.doc: A field multiplicity of [1] must mean a required field, and [0..1] an optional field. A field can have these DSML constraints: minLength, maxLength, minValue, maxValue, pattern, unique, and precision and scale for a Decimal field.
elements.name: dsml025

elements.doc: A relation between entities must be a reference usage typed by the related entity, with the multiplicity [0..1], [1] or [*]. A relation with [*] at the two ends is a many-to-many relation.
elements.name: dsml026

elements.doc: An application must expose an entity with an entity usage that has the keyword #Exposed. Its attribute crud must list the CRUD operations: create, read, update, delete and list.
elements.name: dsml027

elements.doc: A custom operation must be an action definition with the keyword #Operation and typed in and out parameters. The toolchain must not read the body of the action.
elements.name: dsml028

elements.doc: Each operation must have an HTTP method and a path. The DSML must give defaults for CRUD operations. A custom operation must state its method and path.
elements.name: dsml029

elements.doc: A react application must refer to the application whose API it calls, with a dependency that has the #Calls metadata. The two applications then use one API model.
elements.name: dsml030

elements.doc: Phase 2: a view must be a part usage in an application with the keyword #View. Its attribute kind must be list, detail or form. A list or detail view must refer to one entity. A form view must refer to one operation.
elements.name: dsml031

elements.doc: Phase 2: an application can give its navigation as an ordered list of views.
elements.name: dsml032

elements.doc: The roles of a model must be the values of one enumeration definition with the keyword #Roles. Each exposed operation, entity and view must list the roles that can use it in its attribute allowedRoles. The attribute value public = true must mean that no authentication is necessary.
elements.name: dsml033

elements.doc: A destructive database change must have the #Destructive metadata on the changed entity or field. A rename must give the old name in the attribute renamedFrom.
elements.name: dsml034

elements.doc: A logical infrastructure element must be a part usage with one of the logical kinds in the table of the section "Infrastructure layer".
elements.name: dsml035

value.value: No AWS terms in logical layer

elements.doc: A logical element must not contain an AWS term, an AWS attribute or an AWS service name.
elements.name: dsml036

elements.doc: Each logical element must have one AWS realization: a part usage with the matching AWS kind and a dependency with the #Realizes metadata to the logical element.
elements.name: dsml037

elements.doc: An AWS realization must hold the AWS attributes, for example the RDS instance class or the Fargate CPU and memory.
elements.name: dsml038

elements.doc: Each application must be allocated to one logical element with allocate. A fastapi or nextjs application must be allocated to a #ContainerService. A react application must be allocated to a #StaticSite.
elements.name: dsml039

elements.doc: A container service or a static site must refer to each database, user directory and secret store that it uses, with a dependency that has the #Uses metadata.
elements.name: dsml040

elements.doc: An environment must be a part usage with the keyword #Environment. It must have an AWS account ID, an AWS Region and a domain name. The model must contain the environments dev, staging and prod.
elements.name: dsml041

elements.doc: An environment can change only these attributes of an AWS realization: cpu, memory, instanceClass, desiredCount, minCount, maxCount, multiAz and natGatewayCount.
elements.name: dsml042

elements.doc: The model must have one part usage with the keyword #ToolingAccount. It must have the AWS account ID and the AWS Region of the ECR repositories.
elements.name: dsml043

elements.doc: A project must not add a logical kind or an AWS kind. A new kind must come in a new version of the DSML library.
elements.name: dsml044

elements.doc: A verification must be a verification usage with the keyword #Verification. It must have an ID (the short name), a title and a method.
elements.name: dsml045

elements.doc: The attribute method must have one of the values test, analysis, inspection or demonstration.
elements.name: dsml046

elements.doc: A verification must refer to each requirement that it verifies with verify in its objective.
elements.name: dsml047

elements.doc: A verification with the method test must give one or more test file paths, relative to the repository root, in the attribute testFiles.
elements.name: dsml048

elements.doc: A verification can give test case names in the attribute testCases, for example a pytest node ID.
elements.name: dsml049

elements.doc: Each need, requirement and verification must have a short name with the pattern of its kind: N-<NNN>, R-<NNN> or V-<NNN>. <NNN> has three or more digits with leading zeros.
elements.name: dsml050

elements.doc: A project can set different ID patterns in the toolchain configuration file.
elements.name: dsml051

elements.doc: Each short name must be unique in the model. A deleted ID must not be used again.
elements.name: dsml052

elements.doc: Each element without a short name must use its qualified name as its identity.
elements.name: dsml053

elements.doc: An element can have an OpenSysML IdentityMetadata::ElementId annotation. The DSML must not require it.
elements.name: dsml054

elements.doc: A waiver must be a #Waiver metadata usage on the element. It must have the attributes rule (the rule ID), reason and owner. It can have the attribute expires (a date).
elements.name: dsml055

elements.doc: The DSML library must have a semantic version. Each model must state the major and minor version of the library that it uses, with the #DsmlVersion metadata on its root package.
elements.name: dsml056

elements.doc: A minor version of the DSML library must not make a valid model invalid. A major version must come with migration notes.
elements.name: dsml057

elements.doc: The generator must write the folders and root modules of the tree in the section "Output structure and tool compatibility" in the infrastructure output folder of the configuration file.
elements.name: iac001

elements.doc: Each generated HCL file must have a name that ends with .gen.tf. A platform engineer can add hand-written .tf files to a root module, and the generator must not change them.
elements.name: iac002

elements.doc: With the default configuration, the HCL must be valid for the pinned OpenTofu version and for the pinned Terraform version. The required_version constraint must accept the two pinned versions.
elements.name: iac003

elements.doc: A feature of only one tool must be available only through an IaC option in the configuration file, for example OpenTofu state encryption. With such an option, the generator must write a comment that names the one tool that accepts the output.
elements.name: iac004

elements.doc: Each root module must pin the AWS provider to the exact version of the version baseline.
elements.name: iac005

elements.doc: Each root module must use the S3 backend with S3 native state locks (use_lockfile = true) and encryption. The state bucket must be in the AWS account of the root module.
elements.name: iac006

elements.doc: The output must use only aws_* resources and data sources and local modules. It must not use a module from a registry or from a different repository.
elements.name: iac007

elements.doc: HCL addresses must be the snake case of the element names. AWS resource names must have the form <product>-<environment>-<element>. If a name is longer than the AWS limit, the generator must shorten it and add a hash of the full name.
elements.name: iac008

elements.doc: The image of each container service must be a root module variable <application>_image_digest. The CI/CD pipeline must give its value.
elements.name: iac009

elements.doc: Each environment root module must output the values that the pipelines need: the ECS cluster and service names, the API URL, the Cognito user pool ID, app client IDs and login domain, and, in phase 2, the S3 bucket and the CloudFront distribution ID.
elements.name: iac010

elements.doc: Network: the module must write a VPC with a public and a private subnet in each of two or more availability zones, an internet gateway, and the number of NAT gateways that natGatewayCount gives.
elements.name: iac011

elements.doc: Container service: the module must write an ECS cluster, a Fargate service and a task definition with the cpu, memory and desiredCount of the realization. Tasks must be in private subnets with no public IP address.
elements.name: iac012

elements.doc: Container service: the module must write target tracking auto scaling on CPU, between minCount and maxCount.
elements.name: iac013

elements.doc: Container service: the module must write an ALB in the public subnets with an HTTPS listener, an ACM certificate for the API domain, a redirect from HTTP to HTTPS, and a Route 53 record. The target group must use /healthz as the health check.
elements.name: iac014

elements.doc: Container service: the task execution role must permit only image pulls from the tooling ECR repository, reads of the secrets that the service uses, and log writes. The task role must permit only access to the elements that the service uses (#Uses).
elements.name: iac015

elements.doc: Container service: the module must write a CloudWatch log group with a retention of 30 days, and a second task definition that runs the migration command of the application.
elements.name: iac016

elements.doc: Database: the module must write an RDS for PostgreSQL instance in private subnets with the instanceClass and multiAz of the realization, storage encryption with a KMS key, backups for 7 days, and a master password that RDS keeps in Secrets Manager. In prod, deletion protection must be on.
elements.name: iac017

elements.doc: Database: its security group must permit port 5432 only from the security groups of the container services that use it.
elements.name: iac018

elements.doc: User directory: the module must write one Cognito user pool, one app client for each application that uses it (no client secret, authorization code with PKCE, callback URLs on the environment domain), one group for each role value and a managed login domain. Self sign-up must be off.
elements.name: iac019

elements.doc: Secret store: the module must write one Secrets Manager secret and one KMS key for each secret element. The HCL must not contain secret values.
elements.name: iac020

elements.doc: Phase 2, static site: the module must write a private S3 bucket with versioning, a CloudFront distribution with origin access control, an ACM certificate in us-east-1 and a Route 53 alias. CloudFront must return /index.html with HTTP 200 for paths that do not exist.
elements.name: iac021

elements.doc: Tooling: the tooling root module must write one ECR repository for each container application, with immutable tags, scan on push and a lifecycle policy. The repository policy must permit pulls by the task execution roles of the environment accounts.
elements.name: iac022

elements.doc: Each environment root module must call the same local modules. Only the environment attributes of PRD-DSML-042 can make two environments different.
elements.name: iac023

elements.doc: The AWS provider of each root module must set allowed_account_ids to the account ID of its environment or of the tooling account.
elements.name: iac024

elements.doc: The generator must not create AWS accounts. The accounts and AWS Organizations must exist before the bootstrap.
elements.name: iac025

elements.doc: The bootstrap root module of each account must write the state bucket (versioning, encryption, public access blocked), the GitHub OIDC identity provider and the IAM roles for CI.
elements.name: iac026

elements.doc: Each environment account must have a plan role with read-only access, which pull requests can use, and a deploy role, which only the GitHub environment of that account can use. The trust policies must check the repository and the environment in the sub claim.
elements.name: iac027

elements.doc: The tooling account must have a push role, which only workflows of the main branch and of release tags can use.
elements.name: iac028

elements.doc: The bootstrap root module must start with local state. The generator must write a README that gives the command to move that state into the bucket that the module creates.
elements.name: iac029

elements.doc: Each resource that stores data (S3, RDS, Secrets Manager, ECR) must have encryption at rest.
elements.name: iac030

elements.doc: Only ALB listeners and CloudFront distributions can accept traffic from the internet. RDS must have publicly_accessible = false, and each S3 bucket must block public access.
elements.name: iac031

elements.doc: A security group must not permit ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0, except an ALB security group on ports 80 and 443.
elements.name: iac032

elements.doc: An IAM policy must not use the action * or a service wildcard such as s3:*. It can use the resource * only for actions that have no resource-level permissions in AWS.
elements.name: iac033

elements.doc: Each HTTPS listener must use the TLS security policy that the version baseline gives.
elements.name: iac034

elements.doc: The AWS provider of each root module must set default_tags with dsml:product, dsml:environment and dsml:model-commit. Each resource must add the tag dsml:element with the identity of its model element, and dsml:application where an application owns it.
elements.name: iac035

elements.doc: The value of dsml:model-commit must come from the root module variable model_commit at plan time. Generated files must not contain the commit.
elements.name: iac036

elements.doc: If a tag value is longer than the AWS limit of 256 characters, the generator must shorten it and add a hash of the full value.
elements.name: iac037

elements.doc: dsml check-output --infrastructure must run tofu fmt -check, tofu validate (after tofu init -backend=false) and tflint with the AWS rule set on each root module.
elements.name: iac038

elements.doc: The toolchain CI must also run terraform validate on the golden output of each reference model.
elements.name: iac039

elements.doc: An IaC security scan of the golden output must find no finding with high or critical severity. The version baseline gives the scanner.
elements.name: iac040

elements.doc: After an apply, a second tofu plan with the same model and the same commit must show no change.
elements.name: iac041

elements.doc: Container service: the ECS service must ignore changes to its task definition, because the pipeline sets it after the migrations. The service must use the ECS deployment circuit breaker with rollback.
elements.name: iac042

elements.doc: The toolchain must be written in Python, and uv must manage the Python project.
elements.name: top001

elements.doc: The toolchain must install as one Python package that supplies the command dsml.
elements.name: top002

elements.doc: The toolchain must run on the operating systems that decision record 03 gives.
elements.name: top003

elements.doc: Validation, code generation and traceability must not use an AI model.
elements.name: top004

elements.doc: Validation, code generation and trace reports must not use the network. Only the local OpenSysML child process is permitted.
elements.name: top005

elements.doc: The toolchain must not write a secret value to a log, a report or a generated file.
elements.name: top006

elements.doc: Each dependency of the toolchain and of the generated code must have a license that the company accepts for internal software.
elements.name: top007

elements.doc: Generated code must pin each dependency to the exact version that the version baseline gives.
elements.name: top008

elements.doc: The PRD set and the user documentation of the toolchain must use ASD-STE100 Issue 9.
elements.name: top009

elements.doc: Each PRD requirement must have a unique ID with the prefix of its PRD.
elements.name: top010

elements.doc: The DSML appendix must contain each PRD requirement. OpenSysML must parse the appendix with no error.
elements.name: top011

elements.doc: Validation and code generation of a model with 1,000 elements must finish in the time that decision record 03 gives.
elements.name: top012

elements.doc: The model must use these link types: the stakeholder member of a need, frame, #derivation, #refinement, satisfy, allocate, #Realizes and verify.
elements.name: trace001

elements.doc: A satisfy link can come from an application element or from an infrastructure element.
elements.name: trace002

elements.doc: The IR must hold each link with its type and the identities of its source and target.
elements.name: trace003

elements.doc: The traceability engine must follow links in the two directions: from a need to its code, tests and AWS resources, and from a file or resource back to its needs.
elements.name: trace004

elements.doc: Each generated source file that permits comments must start with a header: the line Generated by dsml <major>. Do not edit., then the line Elements: with the identities of its model elements in sorted order.
elements.name: trace005

elements.doc: The generator must write the trace manifest .dsml/trace.gen.json. For each element, it must give each generated file, each symbol in that file (class, function, route or HCL resource address) and the line range of the symbol.
elements.name: trace006

elements.doc: The trace manifest must give the HCL resource addresses of each infrastructure element, so a person can find the AWS resources of an element from its dsml:element tag or from its address.
elements.name: trace007

elements.doc: The trace manifest must be sorted by element identity, then by file path, then by line.
elements.name: trace008

elements.doc: A trace comment must be a line comment with the form trace: <ID>[, <ID>]: # trace: R-001 in Python, HCL and YAML, and // trace: R-001 in TypeScript. An ID can be a short name or a qualified name.
elements.name: trace009

elements.doc: The toolchain must read trace comments in the hand-written files of the output folders and of the test folders in the configuration file. It must not read generated files for trace comments.
elements.name: trace010

elements.doc: A trace comment applies to the next symbol in the file. If no symbol follows, it applies to the file.
elements.name: trace011

elements.doc: The orphan report must list each trace comment with an ID that is not in the model.
elements.name: trace012

elements.doc: dsml trace must write the four reports coverage, orphans, impact and suspect in the table of the section "Reports".
elements.name: trace013

elements.doc: The coverage report must give each requirement one status: missing (no satisfying element), satisfied (a satisfying element, no verification) or verified (a satisfying element and a verification).
elements.name: trace014

elements.doc: An element must count as changed if the hash of its IR form, with no source locations, is different from the hash in the baseline.
elements.name: trace015

elements.doc: The impact and suspect reports must use the baseline that --baseline gives, or the default baseline that decision record 03 gives.
elements.name: trace016

elements.doc: Each report must be available as HTML, CSV and JSON. The HTML report must be one file with no external resources.
elements.name: trace017

elements.doc: Each report must give the model commit and the baseline commit, and no date or time.
elements.name: trace018

elements.doc: Each rule must be Python code that reads only the IR. Each rule must have an ID, a category, a default severity, a message and a fix hint.
elements.name: val001

elements.doc: Rule IDs must have the form <CATEGORY>-<NNN>. A deleted rule ID must not be used again.
elements.name: val002

elements.doc: The severities must be error, warning and info. A finding with the severity error must stop code generation.
elements.name: val003

elements.doc: The configuration file can increase the severity of a rule, or turn off a rule with the default severity warning or info. It must not decrease the severity of a rule with the default severity error or turn it off.
elements.name: val004

elements.doc: The option --fail-on warning must make dsml validate stop with exit code 1 if there is a warning.
elements.name: val005

elements.doc: The validator must write findings as text, as JSON, or as SARIF 2.1.0 with the rule metadata and the source locations.
elements.name: val006

elements.doc: The validator must sort findings by file, line, column and rule ID.
elements.name: val007

elements.doc: The toolchain CI must have, for each rule, one model that the rule accepts and one model that the rule rejects.
elements.name: val008

elements.doc: A #Waiver must stop the findings of its rule on its element only. The report must list waived findings in a separate group, and SARIF must give them as suppressions with the reason.
elements.name: val009

elements.doc: After the expires date of a waiver, its findings must come back, and the validator must report rule STR-014.
elements.name: val010

elements.doc: The identity rules (category IDN) must run only when the user gives --baseline <git-ref> or the configuration file gives a default baseline. The validator must read the baseline model from the local Git repository.
elements.name: val011

elements.doc: The validator must read the result of each formal constraint for each environment from the IR (PRD-CORE-054). It reports rule FCN-001 for a false result and rule FCN-002 for an unknown result.
elements.name: val012

elements.doc: The text rules (category TXT) must be off by default. The configuration file must be able to turn them on.
elements.name: val013

elements.doc: The text rules must use the project dictionary of the top-level PRD as a list of additional approved words. The toolchain must not claim full STE compliance.
elements.name: val014

elements.doc: The validator must contain each rule in the catalog of the section "Rule catalog for phase 1", with its default severity.
elements.name: val015
